questions.question: Q1. Which formula defines the total theoretical energy available for recovery during translational vehicle deceleration?

explanations.a: This represents translational momentum, not kinetic energy.
explanations.b: Kinetic energy is directly proportional to the vehicle mass and the square of its velocity.
explanations.c: This calculates the parallel gravitational force acting along an inclined plane.
explanations.d: This computes the maximum traction force boundary on a flat surface.

questions.question: Q2. How does an increase in the road slope angle (incline) affect the vehicle's normal load force (Fn)?

answers.a: It increases the normal load force.
answers.b: It has no impact on the normal load force.
answers.c: It reduces the normal load force because Fn depends on the cosine of the angle.
answers.d: It causes the normal load force to fluctuate rapidly.

explanations.a: An incline reduces the perpendicular component of gravity pressing the vehicle down.
explanations.b: Normal force varies dynamically with the geometric cosine profile of the slope grade.
explanations.c: As the angle increases, the cosine value decreases, which reduces the normal force pressing the tires against the road surface.
explanations.d: The force shifts smoothly according to the changing trigonometric angle profile.

questions.question: Q3. What occurs physically when the applied braking force (Fb) exceeds the maximum available road traction grip (Fmax)?

answers.b: The vehicle enters a wheel slip state, causing traction loss.
answers.c: The vehicle instantly gains mechanical velocity.
answers.d: The Motor-Generator Unit completely shuts down indefinitely.

explanations.a: Wheel lockup degrades harvesting metrics significantly due to stability penalties.
explanations.b: Exceeding the physical traction limit overcomes static friction, inducing active tire skid or lockup.
explanations.c: Braking force still opposes forward kinetic movement despite traction loss.
explanations.d: The MGU continues running but operates under reduced efficiency constraints.

questions.question: Q4. Why can an electric vehicle's regenerative braking system not harvest all energy during high-force braking events?

answers.a: The vehicle lacks mechanical friction pads.
answers.b: Kinetic energy drops to zero as soon as the brakes are touched.
answers.c: The Motor-Generator Unit (MGU) has a strict physical power/force allocation limit.
answers.d: Battery packs can only accept energy when the vehicle is traveling uphill.

explanations.a: Friction brakes are present to handle excessive torque demands beyond regen capabilities.
explanations.b: Kinetic energy decreases continuously throughout the duration of the stopping cycle.
explanations.c: Any braking force demanded beyond the maximum MGU threshold must be handled by friction brakes, converting that portion to waste heat.
explanations.d: Regenerative capture is functional on any grade, provided the vehicle is actively decelerating.

questions.question: Q5. Which structural factor introduces an efficiency penalty in urban stop-and-go conditions compared to steady state coasting?

answers.a: Frequent blending transitions and high-frequency cycles

explanations.a: Continuous acceleration and deceleration cycles cause conversion losses inside motor controllers and battery chemistry.
explanations.b: Normal loads continue to shift during transient cycling periods.
explanations.c: Urban traffic is characterized by variable velocities rather than constant profiles.
explanations.d: Gravity acts constantly on the vehicle mass regardless of traffic density changes.
